consolidation.en: Board note: Nile Loaf consolidates by FINANCIAL CONTROL. The extra vans are on a short operating lease (we rent them, we drive them).
consolidation.ar: ملاحظة المجلس: نايل لوف تعتمد نهج السيطرة المالية. الفانات الإضافية بعقد تأجير تشغيلي قصير (بنستأجرها وبنسوقها بنفسنا).

sources.T57: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard, Table 5.7 (deck slides 6–7)
sources.T61: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Calculation Guidance, Table 6.1 (deck slide 8)
sources.CORP: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard: direct = owned or operated assets (deck slide 5)
sources.CORP_S1: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, Ch. 4: Scope 1 includes stationary combustion and fugitive (e.g. HFC) emissions
sources.CORP_S2: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, Ch. 4 & Scope 2 Guidance: purchased electricity = Scope 2
sources.S3_T54: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard, Table 5.4: Category 12 End-of-life treatment of sold products
sources.METHODS: GHG Protocol transport methods: fuel-, distance-, spend-based (deck slide 9)
sources.ISO_B41: ISO 14064-1:2018, Annex B.4.1 (leased vehicles depend on consolidation approach)
sources.ISO_B5: ISO 14064-1:2018, Annex B.5 (Category 4: products used by the organization)
sources.ISO_B6: ISO 14064-1:2018, Annex B.6.2 c) (Category 5: end of life of sold products)
sources.EDGAR: JRC/EDGAR, GHG emissions of all world countries, 2024 report
sources.EDGAR_EG: JRC/EDGAR 2024 booklet, Egypt country page (PDF p. 114)
sources.EDGAR_GLOBAL: JRC/EDGAR 2024 booklet, Key conclusions (PDF p. 8) and global per-capita (PDF p. 17)
sources.T57_LEASE: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 2 + Corporate Standard leased-assets guidance (Appendix F): operating lease + financial control → Scope 3 Cat 8; operational control → Scope 1
sources.S2_GUID: GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance (2015): purchased or acquired electricity, steam, heat and cooling = Scope 2
sources.ISO_322: ISO 14064-1:2018, 3.2.2: primary data = a direct measurement, or a calculation based on direct measurements
sources.ISO_323: ISO 14064-1:2018, 3.2.3: site-specific data = primary data obtained within the organizational boundary (all site-specific data are primary)
sources.ISO_324: ISO 14064-1:2018, 3.2.4: secondary data = from sources other than primary data, e.g. databases and published literature

sources.ISO_C5: ISO 14064-1:2018, 3.2.4 + Annex C.5: non-site-specific data include literature data (e.g. default emission factors), calculated data and estimates

name.en: Gas burnt in the bread ovens

desc.en: Natural gas from the city network, burnt in Nile Loaf's own ovens.
desc.ar: غاز طبيعي من شبكة المدينة بيتحرق في أفران نايل لوف نفسها.

reason.en: Combustion in equipment we own = direct = Scope 1.
reason.ar: احتراق في معدات بنملكها = مباشر = النطاق 1.

isoReason.en: Stationary combustion inside our boundary → Category 1.

wisdom.talk: The gas company sold the fuel, but the flame is ours. Whoever burns it reports it as Scope 1.
wisdom.misconception: "We bought the gas, so it's Scope 2." Scope 2 is only purchased electricity, steam, heat or cooling.
wisdom.clause: Corporate Standard Ch. 4: stationary combustion; ISO Annex B.2.2 a)

follow.S2: Ask them: is gas 'purchased energy' like electricity? Where does the CO₂ come out, at the power plant or in our oven?
follow.S3: Ask them: who owns the oven?

desc.en: 6 vans bought by Nile Loaf, fuelled with diesel, delivering bread to shops.
desc.ar: 6 فانات اشترتها نايل لوف، بتمشي بالديزل وبتوزع العيش على الفروع.

reason.en: Fuel used in vehicles we own or control = Scope 1.
reason.ar: وقود في عربيات بنملكها أو نتحكم فيها = النطاق 1.

isoReason.en: Mobile combustion in our own vehicles → Category 1, not Category 3.
isoReason.ar: احتراق متحرك في عربياتنا ← الفئة 1 مش الفئة 3.

wisdom.talk: Transport isn't automatically Scope 3. Table 5.7, row 1: owned or controlled vehicles are Scope 1 for fuel.
wisdom.misconception: "Transport = Scope 3." Ownership and control decide the scope, not the activity.
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 1; ISO B.2.2 b) and B.4.1 (owned transport → Category 1)

follow.S3: Ask them: who owns these vans? Who pays for the diesel?
follow.S2: Ask them: does a diesel van use purchased electricity?

desc.en: Electricity bought from the national grid for mixers, lights, the cold room and A/C.
desc.ar: كهرباء من الشبكة القومية للعجانات والإضاءة وغرفة التبريد والتكييف.

reason.en: Purchased electricity: the CO₂ comes out at the power plant = Scope 2.
reason.ar: كهرباء مشتراة: الانبعاث بيطلع في محطة الكهرباء = النطاق 2.

isoReason.en: Indirect emissions from imported electricity → Category 2.
isoReason.ar: انبعاثات غير مباشرة من كهرباء مستوردة ← الفئة 2.

wisdom.talk: The textbook Scope 2. Companies in markets with contractual instruments (e.g. certificates) must report it two ways: location-based and market-based. We'll see why in the Board Meeting.
wisdom.misconception: "No chimney at our site means no emissions." The chimney is at the power plant, and it's still our responsibility.
wisdom.clause: Scope 2 Guidance (dual reporting); ISO B.3.2 a)

follow.S1: Ask them: where is the smokestack? Inside our walls?
follow.S3: Ask them: is electricity a 'purchased good' (Cat 1) or does it have its own scope?

name.en: Own electric vans charged at the depot
name.ar: فانات كهربا مملوكة بتتشحن في الجراج

desc.en: 2 electric vans owned by Nile Loaf, charged from the grid at our depot.
desc.ar: فانين كهربا ملك نايل لوف، بيتشحنوا من الشبكة في الجراج بتاعنا.

reason.en: Owned vehicle running on electricity = Scope 2 (Table 5.7: Scope 1 for fuel, Scope 2 for electricity).
reason.ar: عربية مملوكة بتمشي بالكهربا = النطاق 2 (جدول 5.7: النطاق 1 للوقود والنطاق 2 للكهربا).

isoReason.en: The emissions are from imported grid electricity → Category 2.
isoReason.ar: الانبعاثات من كهرباء الشبكة المستوردة ← الفئة 2.

wisdom.talk: Same owner, same delivery job as the diesel vans, but a different scope. The energy carrier decides between Scope 1 and Scope 2.
wisdom.misconception: "Electric vans are zero-emission." Their exhaust moved to the power plant.
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 1 ('scope 2 for electricity use'); Calc Guidance Table 6.1 row 1; ISO B.3.2 a). B.4.1's 'owned → Category 1' covers fuel burnt on board, and grid electricity stays Category 2

follow.S1: Ask them: what does an electric van burn on the road?
follow.S3: Ask them: we own it, so why would it be value chain?

name.en: Refrigerant leaking from the cold room
name.ar: تسريب غاز التبريد من غرفة التبريد

desc.en: Our cold room leaks R-134a gas; the technician tops it up every few months.
desc.ar: غرفة التبريد بتسرب غاز R-134a، والفني بيعبيها كل كام شهر.

reason.en: Fugitive emissions from equipment we own = Scope 1.
reason.ar: انبعاثات متسربة من معدات بنملكها = النطاق 1.

wisdom.talk: Nothing burns, but it's still Scope 1. And per kilogram it's a monster: GWP 1,530 means 1 kg of R-134a ≈ 1.5 tonnes of CO₂e.
wisdom.misconception: "No combustion = no emissions" or "it's electricity-related so Scope 2".
wisdom.clause: Corporate Standard Ch. 4 (fugitive); ISO B.2.2 d) NOTE 2 (equipment leaks, e.g. cooling systems); ISO 6.3: use the latest IPCC GWP (AR6)

follow.S2: Ask them: the fridge uses electricity, but is the leaking gas electricity?
follow.S3: Ask them: whose equipment is leaking?

name.en: Leased vans that Nile Loaf drives

desc.en: 3 vans rented on an operating lease. Our drivers, our routes, our diesel.
desc.ar: 3 فانات بعقد تأجير تشغيلي. سواقينا وخطوطنا والديزل علينا.

reason.en: Leased & operated by us, not already in Scope 1/2 → Scope 3 Cat 8 (Table 5.7). That holds because we use financial control. Under operational control they'd be Scope 1.
reason.ar: مستأجرة وبنشغلها ومش محسوبة في النطاق 1/2 ← النطاق 3 فئة 8 (جدول 5.7). ده لأننا بنعتمد السيطرة المالية، ولو السيطرة التشغيلية كانت هتبقى النطاق 1.

isoReason.en: With financial control the fleet is indirect: Category 3 (transport) or 4 (services used, B.5.3). Under operational control it would be Category 1.
isoReason.ar: مع السيطرة المالية الأسطول غير مباشر: الفئة 3 (نقل) أو 4 (خدمات مستخدمة). مع السيطرة التشغيلية هيبقى الفئة 1.

wisdom.talk: This is THE judgment call of the day. Same van, different answer depending on the consolidation approach. That's why the board note told you 'financial control'.
wisdom.misconception: "We drive it, so it's always Scope 1." True under operational control, not under financial control with an operating lease.
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 2 (Cat 8 'not already included in scope 1 or 2') + Corporate Std leased-assets guidance (Appendix F) for the consolidation approach; Calc Guidance Table 6.1 row 4; ISO B.4.1 EXAMPLE, B.5.4 b)

follow.S1: Ask them: who controls the van day to day? And which approach did the board say we use?
follow.S2: Ask them: does this van run on purchased electricity?

desc.en: Our own generator runs on diesel whenever the grid goes down.
desc.ar: المولد بتاعنا بيشتغل ديزل كل ما الكهربا تقطع.

reason.en: We burn the fuel in our own equipment, so it's Scope 1, even though it makes electricity.
reason.ar: إحنا اللي بنحرق الوقود في معداتنا = النطاق 1، حتى لو بيطلع كهربا.

isoReason.en: Stationary combustion in our equipment → Category 1.

wisdom.talk: Electricity you GENERATE yourself from fuel is Scope 1. Only electricity you PURCHASE is Scope 2.
wisdom.misconception: "It produces electricity, so Scope 2."
wisdom.clause: Corporate Standard Ch. 4 (stationary combustion); ISO B.2.1 (stationary sources incl. electricity generators) and B.2.2 a)

follow.S2: Ask them: did we buy this electricity from anyone?
follow.S3: Ask them: whose generator is it?

name.ar: شركة الشحن اللي نايل لوف بتدفعلها

desc.en: 'Wasla Express' delivers our bread to distant shops. Their vans, our invoice.
desc.ar: «وصلة إكسبريس» بتوصل عيشنا للفروع البعيدة. عربياتهم وإحنا اللي بندفع.

reason.en: Transport service we purchase, in vehicles we don't own → Scope 3 Cat 4, even for outbound deliveries.
reason.ar: خدمة نقل بنشتريها في عربيات مش بتاعتنا ← النطاق 3 فئة 4، حتى لو توصيل لبره.

isoReason.en: Freight services paid for by the organization → Category 3.

wisdom.talk: Trap: it's OUTBOUND (to our shops/customers) but it's Cat 4, not Cat 9, because WE pay for it. For sold products going out, who pays decides: we pay → Cat 4, we don't → Cat 9. (Inbound from tier-1 suppliers is Cat 4 regardless.)
wisdom.misconception: "Outbound = downstream = Cat 9." Cat 9 is only transport we don't pay for.
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 7 (purchased transport services incl. outbound logistics = Cat 4); ISO B.4.2 a)

follow.S1: Ask them: whose van is it, and who buys its diesel?
follow.S2: Ask them: is this purchased electricity?

name.en: The mill's truck delivering flour to us

desc.en: Delta Mills (our direct supplier) trucks flour to our bakery. Delivery is invoiced to us.
desc.ar: مطاحن الدلتا (مورّدنا المباشر) بتوصل الدقيق للمخبز. التوصيل عليه فاتورة لينا.

reason.en: Transport between a tier-1 supplier and our operations, in vehicles we don't own → Cat 4.
reason.ar: نقل بين المورد المباشر وعملياتنا في عربيات مش بتاعتنا ← فئة 4.

isoReason.en: Latest transport from supplier to us → Category 3 (upstream transport).
isoReason.ar: آخر نقل من المورد لينا ← الفئة 3 (نقل المنبع).

wisdom.talk: Inbound from a tier-1 supplier = Cat 4. Compare with the next card, the truck one step further upstream.
wisdom.misconception: "It's the supplier's truck, so it's in Cat 1 with the flour." Only transport upstream of tier 1 sits in Cat 1.
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 6 (tier-1 supplier → own operations, vehicles not owned/controlled = Cat 4); ISO B.4.2 a)

follow.S1: Ask them: do we own that truck?

name.en: The truck bringing wheat to the mill

desc.en: A farm cooperative trucks wheat to Delta Mills. We never see this truck.
desc.ar: جمعية زراعية بتنقل القمح لمطاحن الدلتا. إحنا عمرنا ما شفنا العربية دي.

reason.en: Upstream of our tier-1 supplier → already inside the flour's cradle-to-gate footprint → Cat 1.
reason.ar: قبل المورد المباشر ← محسوب أصلاً في بصمة الدقيق من المهد للبوابة ← فئة 1.

isoReason.en: Transport between suppliers is part of purchased goods (Category 4). ISO lets you report all supply-chain transport in Category 3 instead, as long as you don't double count.
isoReason.ar: النقل بين الموردين جزء من السلع المشتراة (الفئة 4). ISO بيسمح بوضع كل نقل سلسلة الإمداد في الفئة 3 بشرط عدم الحساب المزدوج.

wisdom.talk: Same kind of truck as the last card, different category. The tier-2 → tier-1 leg is already in the flour's footprint. Count it twice and you've double counted.
wisdom.misconception: "All upstream trucks are Cat 4." Table 5.7 row 3 puts tier-2 → tier-1 transport in Cat 1.
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 3; ISO B.4.2 a) + Figure B.1 (double counting)

follow.S1: Ask them: is this truck in our building or our fleet?

desc.en: The steel, battery and assembly emissions of the 2 new vans we bought this year.
desc.ar: انبعاثات الحديد والبطارية والتجميع للفانين اللي اشتريناهم السنة دي.

reason.en: Cradle-to-gate emissions of vehicles we purchase → Cat 2 Capital goods.
reason.ar: انبعاثات تصنيع العربيات اللي بنشتريها ← فئة 2 السلع الرأسمالية.

isoReason.en: Capital goods (vehicles) → Category 4, products used by the organization.
isoReason.ar: سلع رأسمالية (عربيات) ← الفئة 4 منتجات بتستخدمها المنظمة.

wisdom.talk: Driving the van is Scope 1 or 2. BUILDING the van is Scope 3 Cat 2, reported in full in the year we buy it (GHG Protocol; ISO B.5.2 b) also allows amortizing it over the asset's life).
wisdom.misconception: "It's our van, so Scope 1." The factory isn't ours. In ISO, someone may quote B.4.1 ('construction of the transport equipment' in Category 3); that refers to third-party transport. Vehicles WE buy are capital goods, B.5.2 b) → Category 4.
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 4 (production of vehicles → Cat 2); ISO B.5.2 b)

follow.S1: Ask them: is the van factory inside our boundary?

name.en: Tanker delivering diesel to our depot

desc.en: The fuel company's tanker truck brings the diesel we later burn in our vans.
desc.ar: عربية شركة البترول بتجيب الديزل اللي بنحرقه بعدين في فاناتنا.

reason.en: Transporting fuels we consume → Cat 3 Fuel- and energy-related activities.
reason.ar: نقل الوقود اللي بنستهلكه ← فئة 3 أنشطة الوقود والطاقة.

isoReason.en: Fuel transportation upstream of our energy → Category 3 (B.4.1). Or count it as the fuel's upstream (Category 4, B.5.2 a)). Choose one and don't double count.
isoReason.ar: نقل الوقود ← الفئة 3 (B.4.1)، أو كجزء من منبع الوقود (الفئة 4، B.5.2 a)). اختار واحدة بس من غير حساب مزدوج.

wisdom.talk: The tricky one. It's transport, but GHG Protocol puts fuel transport in Cat 3, not Cat 4. Burning the diesel is Scope 1, and getting it to us is Cat 3.
wisdom.misconception: "It's a truck delivering to us, so Cat 4." Table 5.7 row 5 has a specific home for transport of fuels and energy.
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 5 ('Transportation of fuels and energy consumed' → Cat 3)

follow.S1: Ask them: do we own the tanker?

name.en: Staff flights to a food trade fair

desc.en: 6 staff fly Cairo ↔ Dubai on a commercial airline for a trade fair.
desc.ar: 6 موظفين مسافرين القاهرة ↔ دبي على خطوط تجارية لمعرض.

reason.en: Employees travelling for business in vehicles operated by third parties → Cat 6.
reason.ar: موظفين مسافرين للشغل في وسائل بيشغلها غيرنا ← فئة 6.

wisdom.talk: Business travel is the classic Cat 6. ISO also lets you include hotel nights linked to the trip.
wisdom.misconception: "We paid for the tickets, so Cat 4." Cat 4 is goods transport; people travelling for work is Cat 6.
wisdom.clause: Calc Guidance Table 6.1 row 2; ISO B.4.2 e)

follow.S1: Ask them: does Nile Loaf own an airline?

desc.en: Bakers take microbuses, the metro or their own cars to and from work.
desc.ar: الخبازين بيركبوا ميكروباص أو مترو أو عربياتهم رايحين جايين الشغل.

reason.en: Transport of employees between home and work → Cat 7.
reason.ar: نقل الموظفين بين البيت والشغل ← فئة 7.

wisdom.talk: Commuting is Cat 7 even though it's employees' own cars, and ISO even allows home-working energy to be considered here.
wisdom.misconception: "Not our cars, not our problem." It's in the value chain.
wisdom.clause: Calc Guidance Table 6.1 row 3; ISO B.4.2 c)

follow.S1: Ask them: who owns the microbus?

name.en: App deliveries the customer pays for

desc.en: Customers order through a delivery app and pay the delivery fee themselves.
desc.ar: العملاء بيطلبوا من أبلكيشن توصيل وبيدفعوا رسوم التوصيل بنفسهم.

reason.en: Transport of sold products to the end consumer, not paid for by us → Cat 9.
reason.ar: نقل منتجاتنا للمستهلك من غير ما إحنا ندفع ← فئة 9.

isoReason.en: Downstream transport not paid for by the organization → Category 3.
isoReason.ar: نقل للمصب مش مدفوع من المنظمة ← الفئة 3.

wisdom.talk: Compare with the courier: same bread, a vehicle we don't own, but the CUSTOMER pays here, so it's Cat 9 instead of Cat 4.
wisdom.misconception: "Cat 4 and 9 depend on direction." For outbound deliveries they depend on who pays, not on direction.
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.7 row 8 ('if not paid for by the reporting company' = Cat 9); ISO B.4.2 b)

follow.S1: Ask them: is the rider on our payroll?

name.en: Customers throwing away our bread bags

desc.en: Plastic and paper bags from our bread end up in household waste.
desc.ar: أكياس البلاستيك والورق بتاعة عيشنا بتخلص في زبالة البيوت.

reason.en: End-of-life of products (incl. packaging) we sold → Cat 12.
reason.ar: نهاية عمر المنتجات (ومنها التغليف) اللي بعناها ← فئة 12.

isoReason.en: End of life of the organization's products → Category 5.

wisdom.talk: Not transport, but here's the bridge to ISO Category 5: the ISO category for the life of our products after we sell them (use and end of life).
wisdom.misconception: "Waste = GHG Protocol Cat 5." Scope 3 Cat 5 is waste from OUR operations; customers' disposal of sold products is Scope 3 Cat 12 (ISO Category 5).
wisdom.clause: Scope 3 Std Table 5.4 (Cat 12); ISO B.6.2 c)

follow.S1: Ask them: is the customer's bin inside our boundary?

name.en: Chilled water bought for the head office

desc.en: Our head office in the New Capital buys chilled water from the district cooling plant next door.
desc.ar: مكتبنا في العاصمة الإدارية بيشتري مياه متلّجة من محطة التبريد المركزي اللي جنبه.

reason.en: Cooling we buy from someone else is purchased energy, like electricity: Scope 2. The emissions happen at the cooling plant, but they exist because we buy that cooling.
reason.ar: التبريد اللي بنشتريه من حد تاني طاقة مشتراة زي الكهربا: نطاق 2. الانبعاثات بتطلع في محطة التبريد، بس هي موجودة عشان إحنا بنشتري التبريد ده.

wisdom.talk: Scope 2 isn't only electricity: steam, heat and cooling you buy count too.
wisdom.misconception: "Cooling isn't electricity, so it must be Scope 3." Purchased cooling is Scope 2.
wisdom.clause: Scope 2 Guidance §1; ISO Annex B.3

follow.S1: Ask them: do we own the chiller plant that makes the cold water?
follow.S3: Ask them: is it a product we buy, or energy we consume?

name.en: Our gas invoices for the ovens

desc.en: Monthly bills from the gas company, with the m³ read from the meter at our bakery.
desc.ar: فواتير شهرية من شركة الغاز، فيها الأمتار المكعبة من العدّاد اللي في مخبزنا.

dReason.en: Invoices come from our meter. Measured at our own asset, inside our boundary, so it's site-specific. It is also primary data: all site-specific data are primary (ISO 14064-1, 3.2.3). Primary = half points, site-specific = full points.
dReason.ar: الفواتير جاية من عدّادنا. متقاسة عند حاجة بتاعتنا جوه حدودنا، يبقى بيانات خاصة بالموقع. وهي كمان بيانات أولية: كل البيانات الخاصة بالموقع أولية (ISO 14064-1، 3.2.3). «أولية» = نص الدرجة، «خاصة بالموقع» = الدرجة كاملة.

wisdom.talk: Invoices are the classic primary data. The sharper word is site-specific: the meter is ours, inside our boundary.
wisdom.misconception: "An invoice is just paperwork, so it's secondary." The number on it is a direct measurement at our own meter.

follow.S: Ask them: who measured these m³, and where is that meter?
follow.P: Good instinct! Now: is the meter inside or outside our boundary?

name.en: The DESNZ conversion factor for diesel

desc.en: 2.66 kg CO₂e per litre, taken from the UK government's published factor database.
desc.ar: 2.66 كجم CO₂e لكل لتر، من قاعدة بيانات المعاملات المنشورة بتاعة الحكومة البريطانية.

dReason.en: Nobody measured this for us. It comes from a published database, so it's secondary data (ISO 14064-1, 3.2.4). It's the 'conversion' step that turns our litres into CO₂e.
dReason.ar: محدش قاسه عشاننا. ده من قاعدة بيانات منشورة، يبقى بيانات ثانوية (ISO 14064-1، 3.2.4). ده خطوة «التحويل» اللي بتحوّل اللترات بتاعتنا لـ CO₂e.

wisdom.talk: Most inventories mix the two: primary activity data (our litres) × a secondary factor (DESNZ).
wisdom.misconception: "It's an official government number, so it's primary." Official ≠ primary. It wasn't measured from our activity.

follow.SS: Ask them: was this number measured at our bakery?
follow.P: Ask them: who measured it, and was it measured from our activity?

name.en: Fuel the courier actually burnt for us
name.ar: الوقود اللي شركة الشحن حرقته فعلاً عشاننا

desc.en: Wasla Express sends us the litres from its own fuel logs for the trips that carried our bread.
desc.ar: «وصلة إكسبريس» بتبعتلنا اللترات من سجلات الوقود بتاعتها للرحلات اللي شالت عيشنا.

dReason.en: It's a direct measurement, so it's primary (3.2.2). But the courier collected it, outside our organizational boundary, so it's not site-specific (3.2.3).
dReason.ar: دي قياسات مباشرة، يبقى بيانات أولية (3.2.2). بس اللي جمعها شركة الشحن، بره حدود مؤسستنا، يبقى مش خاصة بالموقع (3.2.3).

wisdom.talk: This is the gold standard for Scope 3: real measured data from the supplier, instead of averages.
wisdom.misconception: "It's about our bread, so it's site-specific." The vans and the fuel logs are the courier's, not ours.

follow.SS: Ask them: whose vans, whose fuel logs? Inside or outside our boundary?
follow.S: Ask them: is this from a database, or from real fuel logs?

desc.en: Our maintenance team reads the kWh on the bakery's own meter every month.
desc.ar: فريق الصيانة بيقرا الكيلووات ساعة من عدّاد المخبز كل شهر.

dReason.en: Read directly from our own meter. Measured at our own asset, inside our boundary, so it's site-specific. It is also primary data: all site-specific data are primary (ISO 14064-1, 3.2.3). Primary = half points, site-specific = full points.
dReason.ar: متقرية مباشرة من عدّادنا. متقاسة عند حاجة بتاعتنا جوه حدودنا، يبقى بيانات خاصة بالموقع. وهي كمان بيانات أولية: كل البيانات الخاصة بالموقع أولية (ISO 14064-1، 3.2.3). «أولية» = نص الدرجة، «خاصة بالموقع» = الدرجة كاملة.

wisdom.talk: Same family as the invoices: direct measurement at our own site.
wisdom.misconception: "The grid emissions happen at the power plant, so the data is secondary." The kWh is measured here; the grid factor is the secondary part.

follow.S: Ask them: where does the kWh number come from?
follow.P: Close! Is this meter inside our boundary?

name.en: Default fridge leak rate from IPCC guidelines
name.ar: معدل تسريب افتراضي للتلاجات من إرشادات IPCC

desc.en: We have no refill records for the old shop fridges, so we use a % per year leak rate from the IPCC guidelines.
desc.ar: معندناش سجلات تعبئة للتلاجات القديمة في المحلات، فبنستخدم نسبة تسريب سنوية من إرشادات IPCC.

dReason.en: A default value from published literature, not a measurement of our fridges: secondary data. ISO Annex C.5 names 'literature data (e.g. default emission factors)'.
dReason.ar: قيمة افتراضية من مراجع منشورة، مش قياس لتلاجاتنا: بيانات ثانوية. ملحق ISO C.5 بيذكر «بيانات المراجع (زي معاملات الانبعاث الافتراضية)».

wisdom.talk: Defaults are fine when measuring isn't practical, but they should be recorded and justified.
wisdom.misconception: "It's about our own fridges, so it's site-specific." The subject is ours, but the number isn't measured.

follow.SS: Ask them: did anyone weigh the gas that went into those fridges?
follow.P: Ask them: was this measured by anyone, or is it a default from a book?

name.en: Delta Mills' footprint per tonne of flour

desc.en: Our flour supplier calculated it from its own metered gas and electricity, and shared the result with us.
desc.ar: مورّد الدقيق حسبها من الغاز والكهربا المتقاسة عنده، وبعتلنا النتيجة.

dReason.en: A calculation based on direct measurements is primary data (3.2.2). The meters belong to the mill, outside our boundary, so it's not site-specific.
dReason.ar: حساب مبني على قياسات مباشرة = بيانات أولية (3.2.2). العدّادات بتاعة المطحنة، بره حدودنا، يبقى مش خاصة بالموقع.

wisdom.talk: Primary data can be an emission factor too, not only activity data (3.2.2, Note 1).
wisdom.misconception: "It's a calculated number, so it's secondary." A calculation from direct measurements is still primary.

follow.S: Ask them: is this an industry average, or the mill's own measured energy?
follow.SS: Ask them: whose meters produced this number?

name.en: Average commute taken from a published study
name.ar: متوسط مسافة المواصلات من دراسة منشورة

desc.en: We didn't survey staff; we multiply headcount by the average km per worker from a published transport study.
desc.ar: ماعملناش استبيان للموظفين؛ بنضرب عدد الموظفين في متوسط الكيلومترات للعامل من دراسة نقل منشورة.

dReason.en: An estimate built from published literature, not measured from our staff: secondary data (ISO 14064-1, 3.2.4; Annex C.5 'estimates').
dReason.ar: تقدير مبني على مراجع منشورة، مش متقاس من موظفينا: بيانات ثانوية (ISO 14064-1، 3.2.4؛ ملحق C.5 «تقديرات»).

wisdom.talk: A staff survey would turn this into primary data and lower the uncertainty.
wisdom.misconception: "Headcount is our own data, so the whole thing is site-specific." The km per worker is a literature average.

follow.SS: Ask them: did we ask our own staff how far they travel?
follow.P: Ask them: who measured these kilometres?

name.en: Technician's refill log for our cold room

desc.en: Kilograms of R-134a the technician weighed into our cold room, written in our logbook.
desc.ar: كيلوجرامات R-134a اللي الفني وزنها وعبّاها في غرفة التبريد، ومكتوبة في سجلنا.

dReason.en: Weighed at our own cold room. Measured at our own asset, inside our boundary, so it's site-specific. It is also primary data: all site-specific data are primary (ISO 14064-1, 3.2.3). Primary = half points, site-specific = full points.
dReason.ar: متوزنة عند غرفة التبريد بتاعتنا. متقاسة عند حاجة بتاعتنا جوه حدودنا، يبقى بيانات خاصة بالموقع. وهي كمان بيانات أولية: كل البيانات الخاصة بالموقع أولية (ISO 14064-1، 3.2.3). «أولية» = نص الدرجة، «خاصة بالموقع» = الدرجة كاملة.

wisdom.talk: Compare with the IPCC default card: same topic, very different data quality.
wisdom.misconception: "The technician is a contractor, so it's not site-specific." What counts is where it was measured: our own cold room.

follow.S: Ask them: was this weighed, or taken from a book?
follow.P: Close! Where is the cold room, inside or outside our boundary?

name.en: Bag maker's measured energy per 1,000 bags
name.ar: طاقة مصنع الأكياس المتقاسة لكل 1000 كيس

desc.en: The packaging supplier meters the electricity its machines use and gives us the kWh per 1,000 bags.
desc.ar: مورّد التغليف بيقيس كهربا مكناته وبيدّينا الكيلووات ساعة لكل 1000 كيس.

dReason.en: Directly measured, so primary (3.2.2). Collected at the supplier's factory, outside our boundary, so not site-specific (3.2.3).
dReason.ar: متقاسة مباشرة، يبقى أولية (3.2.2). اتجمعت في مصنع المورّد، بره حدودنا، يبقى مش خاصة بالموقع (3.2.3).

wisdom.talk: Supplier-specific primary data beats a database average for the same material.
wisdom.misconception: "Anything from a supplier is secondary." Secondary means databases and literature, not 'someone else measured it'.

follow.S: Ask them: is this from a database, or from the supplier's own meters?
follow.SS: Ask them: whose factory is it?

from.en: Misr Fuel Station – Fleet Card statement 2026
from.ar: محطة وقود مصر – كشف كارت الأسطول 2026

wisdom.talk: Fuel-based method with primary data: litres from the fuel card. The best data you'll ever get for Scope 1 transport.
wisdom.misconception: Using the EGP amount instead of litres. Spend is the weakest proxy.
wisdom.clause: Deck slide 9: fuel-based method; factor DESNZ 2025

from.en: North Cairo Electricity Distribution Co. – Annual statement
from.ar: شركة شمال القاهرة لتوزيع الكهرباء – كشف سنوي

wisdom.talk: Location-based Scope 2 with Egypt's grid average. The EV chargers are in here: that's where the electric vans' emissions went.
wisdom.misconception: Forgetting the EV sub-meter, or adding the generator's diesel here (that's Scope 1).
wisdom.clause: Scope 2 Guidance (location-based); EEHC 2024/25 grid factor

from.en: CoolTech Services – Refrigerant top-up log, cold room #1
from.ar: كول تك للخدمات – سجل تعبئة غاز التبريد، غرفة 1

wisdom.talk: 42 kg of gas becomes 64 tonnes of CO₂e. Many students forget the GWP. Assumption: what we topped up equals what leaked.
wisdom.misconception: Reporting 42 kg as 0.042 t, i.e. forgetting × GWP.
wisdom.clause: IPCC AR6 GWP100 for HFC-134a = 1,530; screening method (top-up = leak)

from.en: Travel desk – Trade fair trip sheet

wisdom.talk: Two traps: forgetting the return leg, and forgetting it's per passenger. Also: this factor excludes radiative forcing. With RF it'd be noticeably higher.
wisdom.misconception: 6 × 2,420 (forgot return) or 2 × 2,420 (forgot passengers).
wisdom.clause: Calc Guidance Table 6.1 (Cat 6); DESNZ 2025 air factor

from.en: Wasla Express – Annual service invoice to Nile Loaf
from.ar: وصلة إكسبريس – فاتورة الخدمة السنوية لنايل لوف

k.en: Diesel used on Nile Loaf routes
k.ar: ديزل مستهلك على خطوط نايل لوف

hint.en: EGP → USD (÷ 50), then × kg CO₂e per USD
hint.ar: جنيه ← دولار (÷ 50) وبعدين × كجم لكل دولار

wisdom.talk: Same trips, three answers: 12.8, 16.0, 19.6 t. The fuel-based number uses the courier's own data. Spend-based uses a US trucking-industry average per dollar and gets inflation and exchange rates mixed in. That's why the methods form a data-quality hierarchy.
wisdom.misconception: "Pick the highest to be conservative" or "they're all equally valid". Use the most specific data you can get and disclose the method.
wisdom.clause: Deck slide 9 (methods); GHG Protocol Scope 3 Calc Guidance Ch. 4 (Cat 4 methods)

prefilled.calc: 1,200 t flour × 0.45 kg CO₂e/kg (Delta Mills declaration, fictional)

boardModel.note: Game assumptions for Chapter 4 (see FACTORS.md). Teams are ranked on LOCATION-based reduction; market-based shown alongside.

ceo.en: Drag each emission source into the right basket: Scope 1, 2 or 3.
ceo.ar: اسحب كل مصدر انبعاثات للسلة الصح: نطاق 1 أو 2 أو 3.

hint.en: Direct: what we own or control burns or leaks
hint.ar: مباشر: اللي بنملكه أو بنتحكم فيه بيحرق أو بيسرّب

hint.en: Energy we buy: electricity, steam, heat, cooling
hint.ar: طاقة بنشتريها: كهربا، بخار، حرارة، تبريد

hint.en: Everything else in our value chain
hint.ar: كل حاجة تانية في سلسلة القيمة

title.en: Activity 2 · What kind of data is it?

ceo.en: Drag each piece of data into its basket. Ask: who measured it, and where?
ceo.ar: اسحب كل معلومة للسلة بتاعتها. اسأل: مين قاسها، وفين؟

hint.en: Primary data measured inside our own boundary
Measured directly, but outside our boundary

hint.ar: من قواعد بيانات ومراجع وقيم افتراضية وتقديرات

takeaways.en: Ownership and control decide the scope: what we own or control and burn is Scope 1, energy we buy is Scope 2, the rest of the value chain is Scope 3.
takeaways.ar: الملكية والسيطرة هي اللي بتحدد النطاق: اللي بنملكه أو بنتحكم فيه وبيحرق = نطاق 1، الطاقة اللي بنشتريها = نطاق 2، وباقي سلسلة القيمة = نطاق 3.

takeaways.en: Primary data come from a direct measurement, or a calculation based on one. When it's measured inside our own boundary (our invoices, our meters), it's site-specific. All site-specific data are primary.
takeaways.ar: البيانات الأولية جاية من قياس مباشر أو حساب مبني عليه. ولو متقاسة جوه حدودنا (فواتيرنا وعدّاداتنا) تبقى خاصة بالموقع. وكل البيانات الخاصة بالموقع أولية.

takeaways.en: Secondary data come from databases and published literature, like conversion factors and defaults. Use them when measuring isn't practical, and record where they came from.
takeaways.ar: البيانات الثانوية جاية من قواعد البيانات والمراجع المنشورة، زي معاملات التحويل والقيم الافتراضية. نستخدمها لما القياس مايبقاش عملي، ونسجّل مصدرها.
